title: Nvidia posts $96.2B quarter and says it has supply for another 70% growth year
subtitle: Q2 FY27 revenue doubled year over year, AWS committed to buy two million GPUs, and Jensen Huang told analysts hyperscaler capex will hit $1.3T in 2027.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Nvidia reported second-quarter FY27 results after the close on August 26, with revenue of $96.2 billion — up 106% from a year ago — and earnings of $2.22 per share, more than double the year-ago figure. On the analyst call, CEO Jensen Huang told listeners the company already has the supply to grow revenue another 70% in fiscal 2028, well above sell-side consensus. CFO Colette Kress said combined capex from the top five hyperscalers is on track to reach $1.3 trillion in 2027, up from roughly $800 billion this year. Alongside the print, Nvidia and Amazon announced that AWS will buy two million Nvidia GPUs and adopt Nvidia's new Vera CPU across its infrastructure.

The Vera piece is the most consequential detail. AWS has spent years building its own Graviton and Trainium silicon; committing to a Nvidia general-purpose CPU inside its data centers is a reversal in direction, and it hands Nvidia the missing piece of the rack — the host processor sitting next to the GPUs — inside the largest cloud in the world. The two-million-GPU order also puts a number on how deep the training and inference buildout still goes, at a moment when several public-market observers are asking whether the capex cycle has topped out.

The report lands in the same 48 hours as OpenAI's Jalapeño benchmark disclosures and Intel's Hot Chips presentations, both of which position custom inference silicon as a threat to Nvidia's margin structure. Nvidia's answer, quarter after quarter, has been that training demand is inelastic and that its full-stack advantage — CUDA, NVLink, and now Vera — keeps the top of the market. So far the earnings keep confirming that story: 106% year-over-year growth is not the shape of a plateau.

For learners: when a company doubles revenue and forecasts another 70% next year, the interesting question is not whether the market is big. It is what supplier the market depends on, and how many alternatives that supplier has coming. Every large-cap AI story right now — hyperscaler capex, custom chips, sovereign-AI deals — routes back through Nvidia's guidance line. Learn to read that line first.
